lines.text: Here is [[f|$\sin x$]]. What is its [[d|slope]] at each point?
lines.say: Here's sine x. What is its slope at each point?

lines.text: Slide a tangent along the wave, and plot each slope as a [[d|teal dot]].
lines.say: Slide a tangent along the wave, and plot each slope as a dot.

lines.text: The slopes trace a wave of their own. It is exactly [[d|$\cos x$]].
lines.say: The slopes trace a wave of their own. It's exactly cosine x.

lines.text: At 0 the slope is 1: chapter 4's limit, $\frac{\sin h}{h} \to 1$, is this very slope.
lines.say: At zero the slope is one. Chapter four's limit is this very slope.

lines.text: Why cosine? Put a point on a circle of radius 1, at angle $\theta$.
lines.say: Why cosine? Put a point on a circle of radius one, at angle theta.

lines.text: Its height is [[f|$\sin\theta$]]. Its distance across is $\cos\theta$.
lines.say: Its height is sine theta. Its distance across is cosine theta.

lines.text: Turn the angle steadily: the point moves at speed 1, along the [[d|tangent]].
lines.say: Turn the angle steadily, and the point moves at speed one, along the tangent.

lines.text: Its velocity makes a triangle: the radius triangle, turned a [[w|quarter turn]].
lines.say: Its velocity makes a triangle: the radius triangle, turned a quarter turn.

lines.text: So the height grows at rate [[d|$\cos\theta$]], and the distance across at [[a|$-\sin\theta$]].
lines.say: So the height grows at rate cosine theta, and the distance across at minus sine theta.
Keep differentiating: sine, cosine, minus sine, minus cosine, and sine again.

lines.text: Each derivative slides the wave a [[w|quarter period]] left. Four steps make a full circle.
lines.say: Each derivative slides the wave a quarter period left. Four steps make a full circle.

lines.text: Two steps give [[a|$-\sin x$]]: the second derivative is minus the function itself.
lines.say: Two steps give minus sine: the second derivative is minus the function itself.

lines.text: That is the law of a spring, $x'' = -x$: why sine waves describe everything that [[w|oscillates]].
lines.say: That's the law of a spring, which is why sine waves describe everything that oscillates.
Sine's slope is cosine, cosine's is minus sine. Each derivative is a quarter turn.
